title: What Is the Best Customer Feedback Solution for a Regulated Industry?
summary: The best feedback solution for a regulated industry pairs audited security with traceable, consistent AI analysis. What to require and how to test vendors.
body_markdown:
Banks, insurers, healthcare networks, utilities and telcos have the same feedback problem as everyone else, with two extra constraints. Regulators expect you to evidence what customers are experiencing, not just report a score. And every vendor that touches customer comments becomes part of your security and compliance perimeter.


The best customer feedback solution for a regulated industry passes your security review and produces analysis you can defend to an auditor. That means independently audited security controls, no training on your data, and AI themes that trace back to the exact comments behind them. Thematic is built for this. It holds System and Organization Controls (SOC 2) Type II certification. It never uses customer data to train models for other clients. And it links every theme to the comments behind it, so analysts can review and correct the results.


Below is what "regulated-ready" actually means, what regulators are asking for, where most feedback tools fall short, and a checklist you can use in your next vendor evaluation.


## What does "regulated-ready" mean for customer feedback analytics?


A regulated-ready feedback solution is one that meets two bars at once: the security bar your risk team sets, and the evidence bar your regulator sets. Most buyer guides only cover the first.


It often gets confused with "has a[SOC 2 report](https://getthematic.com/insights/vendor-security-certifications) ." Certification is necessary, but it says nothing about whether the analysis itself is accurate or explainable.


A regulated-ready solution covers five dimensions:


- **Security controls:** independently audited controls, encryption, access management and data isolation.
- **Data governance:** clear rules on where data is hosted, how long it is kept and whether it trains anyone's models.
- **Accuracy:** themes that reflect what customers actually said, measured on your own data.
- **Consistency:** the same question returns the same answer next month, so trends are real.
- **Traceability:** every finding links back to source comments a reviewer can read.


This matters because a feedback program in a regulated business is a governance tool. If you can't show how a conclusion was reached, it won't hold up in a board pack or a regulatory review.


## What do regulators expect from customer feedback programs?


Regulators increasingly expect firms to monitor real customer outcomes using a broad set of signals.


**Outcomes monitoring.** Under the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) Consumer Duty, a firm "[must regularly monitor the outcomes retail customers](https://www.handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/PRIN/2A/9.html) " receive across products, communications and support. In its[review of insurers](https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/multi-firm-reviews/insurance-multi-firm-review-outcomes-monitoring-under-consumer-duty) , the FCA said firms "must regularly assess, test, understand and evidence the outcomes their customers are receiving."


**Broader sources than complaints and NPS.** The same review warned that "focusing too much on complaints pushes responsibility on to customers" and criticized firms that were highly reliant on net promoter score (NPS). Stronger approaches drew on a wide range of feedback sources.


**Segment-level evidence.** The FCA noted it "did not consistently see firms demonstrating monitoring of the outcomes experienced by distinct groups of customers." That requires breaking open-text feedback down by segment, not just reading the topline.


**Scale.** In the US, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau received[more than 6.6 million complaints in 2025](https://bankingjournal.aba.com/2026/04/cfpb-received-6-6m-consumer-complaints-in-2025/) , roughly double the 2024 total.


**Data protection.** The[General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj) requires personal data to be "limited to what is necessary" and processed with "appropriate security." In US healthcare, the[Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/laws-regulations/index.html) governs protected health information and the vendors that handle it.


## Where do most customer feedback tools fall short?


Most tools fall short on accuracy and explainability, not on certifications.


- [Black-box themes](https://getthematic.com/insights/auditable-transparent-ai-feedback-analytics) **.** The tool reports a topic but can't show which comments produced it.
- **Inconsistent answers.** General-purpose large language models (LLMs) can give different answers to the same question, which breaks month-over-month tracking.
- **Confabulation.** The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)[defines confabulation](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf) as "the production of confidently stated but erroneous or false content." In a regulated report, that is a compliance risk, not a quirk.
- **Unclear data use.** Some tools pool customer data to improve shared models.
- **Partial understanding.** A[Bank of England and FCA survey](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/report/2024/artificial-intelligence-in-uk-financial-services-2024) found 46% of UK financial services firms reported only "partial understanding" of the AI they use, much of it from third parties.


One demo-time test: ask the vendor to run the same analysis twice on your data and show you the comments behind the top three themes. If the answers differ or the evidence is thin, the tool won't survive an audit.


## How does Thematic meet security and accuracy requirements in regulated industries?


**Audited security.** Thematic holds[SOC 2 Type II certification](https://getthematic.com/product/security-and-compliance) covering security, availability and confidentiality, audited annually by A-LIGN. Thematic also completes annual third-party penetration tests.


**No training on your data.** Thematic does not use customer data to train models that benefit other clients, and there is no cross-client learning. Thematic only uses LLMs where it can guarantee how data is retained and used.


**Data isolation and residency.** Thematic isolates each customer's data at the database level and hosts data in the customer's preferred geographic region to meet data residency requirements. Data is encrypted at rest and in transit.


**Access control and audit trails.** Thematic supports role-based access control, SAML 2.0 single sign-on and full logging, so every user action is traceable.


**Minimal personal data.** Thematic analyzes the feedback text itself, so teams can leave personal identifiers out of their uploads, which supports GDPR data minimization. For personally identifiable information (PII) inside comments, Thematic offers redaction at ingestion as a paid, best-effort add-on.


**Traceable, editable themes.** Every theme in Thematic links to the customer comments behind it. Analysts can review, merge and correct themes, so the taxonomy reflects how your business talks about its products.


**Consistency over time.** Thematic maintains a stable theme taxonomy. A change in a theme's volume or impact reflects a change in customer experience, not a change in the model. Thematic's themes reach[80 to 90% accuracy](https://getthematic.com/insights/ai-feedback-analytics-accuracy) before any human refinement, while expert human coders agree with each other only 40 to 70% of the time.


## What does this look like in practice?


[A large financial services provider](https://getthematic.com/case-studies/financial-services) was sitting at a negative NPS on under a hundred responses a month. Using Thematic's[score-change waterfall](https://getthematic.com/insights/quantify-themes-moved-nps-score) , the insights team found that client communications was worth roughly 7 points and the customer experience (CX) and contact team roughly 8 points. Each department could finally see its own contribution. After acting on those drivers, NPS improved by more than 20 points, moving from negative to positive.


The same team tested the alternative. An analyst built an NPS agent on an enterprise LLM in about an hour. It produced plausible themes but could not give the same answer twice, build the waterfall or maintain the taxonomy. Technology leadership chose to buy for standalone functions and build only where a capability is hard to separate from core systems. Thematic is now their consistent source of truth, with LLMs as the interface on top via Model Context Protocol (MCP).


**Community Health System** , a not-for-profit healthcare network in California, used Thematic to analyze open-ended employee engagement feedback across 250 departments. The team produced[250 one-page department reports](https://getthematic.com/insights/community-health-systems-actionable-insights) in a three-day sprint and saved more than 160 hours, about $10,000, per cycle.


**A large water utility** used Thematic to analyze monthly NPS survey comments through a storm-driven service crisis and returned to benchmark service levels within a few months.


## A buyer's checklist for regulated industries


1. Can you share a current SOC 2 Type II report, and which trust criteria does it cover?
2. Will our data ever train models used by other customers?
3. Where will our data be hosted, and can we choose the region?
4. Do you need PII to run the analysis, and can it be redacted at ingestion?
5. Can every theme be traced back to the source comments?
6. Can our analysts edit and approve the theme taxonomy?
7. Does the same analysis return the same answer when rerun?
8. Can you break results down by customer segment and product?


## The short answer


The best customer feedback solution for a regulated industry combines audited security with analysis you can defend. Thematic pairs SOC 2 Type II controls and no training on customer data with traceable, analyst-editable themes that stay consistent over time. To test any vendor, run the same analysis twice on your own data and ask to see the comments behind each finding.
